independent_pure_probes.scope: Synthetic opaque word fixtures only. Probe passes establish observations, not prototype qualification.

checks.conclusion: Finite normal/zero expressions agree with source, including left-associated dt*dt*k, separately rounded additions and inclusive utils::inv threshold.
Integration inverse uses exactly dt==0 then +0; other finite dt uses 1/dt. It must not be replaced by utils::inv. Both signed dt zeros match the source prototype.
Manual strict finite comparisons preserve equal signed zero, matching native f32::clamp. The generic impulse clamp chooses a boundary for equality and must not be reused here.
Conditional positional RHS term, unary negation of effective velocity, copied RHS/RHS-without-bias and ForceBased versus AccelerationBased CFM placement match covered source formulas.
Both positive and negative zero ceilings/durations preserve native multiplication/unary-negation bound words; expected outputs compare literal words.

required_pre_data_corrections.severity: Prospective return-contract defect, not an engine defect
required_pre_data_corrections.finding: inverse_duration_word is a captured computed output but is included in arithmetic_inputs. With all true inputs finite, a NaN captured inverse is classified as nonfinite_arithmetic_input and no mismatch is retained; RHS NaN already produces MISMATCH.
required_pre_data_corrections.correction: Remove inverse_duration_word from input-domain accounting while retaining strict word parsing and output equality. Nonfinite captured outputs for eligible true inputs must remain mismatches.

required_pre_data_corrections.finding: Finite normal h=k=0x7f7fffff produces overflow in h*k. The helper marks overflow but inverse attempts exact(infinity), raising ValueError with no structured exclusion result returned.
required_pre_data_corrections.correction: Retain an explicit arithmetic-domain exclusion/failure record carrying the captured inputs/outputs and accumulated exclusions. Do not swallow malformed schema or other errors into PASS.

scope_and_freeze_requirements: This is a draft narrow ERP/RHS/CFM/bounds verifier, not a frozen preregistration, collector, complete construction-row or cohort/replay admission verifier.

The prototype intentionally does not validate row identity, native frame/DOF, full J/W blocks, solver offsets, initial impulse +0, or inv_lhs=utils::inv(actual solved weighted selector). Synthetic inconsistent extra fields still receive narrow DECLARED_FORMULAS_MATCH; a future exact schema and source-bound producer must reject them before any whole-construction claim.

The cap/model currently come from the nested row; future producer/reader must bind them independently to the actual JointMotor.max_force/model and MotorParameters.max_impulse/target fields at the build site, so a self-consistent but wrong cap cannot masquerade as source fidelity.

Actual full event order evaluates max_impulse and bounds before RHS; the prototype evaluates independent bound multiplication afterward. Covered output words agree, but operation_count is not a native ordered-operation trace. Either match this order before freeze or limit the claim to each expression order.

Nonnegative duration/cap and finite-normal-or-zero qualification restrictions are reader eligibility choices; source consistency alone does not establish valid physical gains or plant accuracy. Native nonfinite limit/cap cases are conservatively excluded, not interpreted as zero.

Before collection freeze actual constructor locals, availability, every expected slice/build, joint/root/cache identity, endpoint timing, source/features/compiler/environment flags, binary and complete-failure retention. BeforePositionIntegration must be the actual copied multibody velocity before q advance, not final stabilized velocity.

No runtime floating point mode/MXCSR/FTZ/DAZ, private-cache full state equivalence, RHS-origin/contact attribution, physical motor accuracy, solver convergence, candidate adoption or maturity claim is established.
review_versioning: Only the preserved initial prototype is reviewed. Any subsequent repair or integration helper needs its own source/tamper review; this receipt cannot qualify later bytes.
